title: Shiva Purana Vol. 3 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §5C desert and intention, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Machine and the Amnesty
concepts.description: **nineteen chapters cancel karma outright on at least five currencies** — vrata, accident, bare favour, austerity, death in battle — against four chapters whose rule is that nothing expires and whose jurisdiction map divides guru, king and Yama **with no slot for the pardoning power.** ⛑ **Ch 413 is the only place the override is argued**: Brahmā makes the moral case in full, Devī concedes every word and asserts refuge alone, **and Brahmā then argues her case back for a page, ending at *"You are also the one who establishes good deeds and bad deeds"* — the categories he prosecuted under withdrawn from underneath his own objection.** Five reconciliations in five chapters, none referencing another: refuge, a mantra-key, ritual exhaustion that *satisfies* ch 320's rule rather than overriding it, purgation inside Śiva's own world, and a twelve-year term. Withdraws this build's "never in the same sentence" formulation, which ch 435 falsifies. Carries Īśvara's own account of the apparatus as scaffolding, and the same build-then-void architecture applied to **effort** at ch 420's twelve-tier saṅkalpa — with ch 441's non-collapsing japa menu recorded as a negative

concepts.title: The Vrata He Did Not Know He Was Doing
concepts.description: a hunter waiting to shoot deer dislodges water and bilva leaves onto an unnoticed liṅgam **four times, in the vigil's four watches, with its correct offerings** — so the accident reproduces the rite's *content*, not merely its outcome. The deer's plea lands (*"filled with wonder"*) and **the next clause credits the worship instead.** Śiva calls it ***"your vrata."*** And the closing sentence makes the involuntariness the **minor premise of an *a fortiori* argument** for Śivarātri. Also: **Guha is one of only two of the volume's seventeen name-etiologies not derived from damage**, and the volume contains a second Guha with no note distinguishing them

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 3 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §5J doctrine and practice, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Four Śaiva Paths
concepts.description: **Śaiva Siddhānta, the Pāśupata vow, the great vratas and the *kāpālika mode*, named and accepted**, with dakṣiṇa and beyond-dakṣiṇa (*"There is no conflict with them"*), Sāṃkhya/Vaiśeṣika/Yoga/Nyāya *"virtuous and distinguished"*, and the Śiva Āgamas cited *"divided into four categories, Kamika and the others."* ⚑ **But every clause is a request for *permission*, and each grant of standing carries *"controlled by Shiva's commands."*** A clearance procedure, not a tolerance statement. The exclusion list contains **no birth category**. Also corroborates the Pāśupata lineage's endpoints across volumes — *"starting with Shveta and ending with Nakulisha"* — while its arithmetic disagrees

concepts.title: The Doxography
concepts.description: ~30 paired positions on Śiva, unranked and unattributed, diagnosed **epistemically**: *"Because of their different conceptions and beliefs, **sages** are unable to grasp his true nature."* The inverse of the inexpressibility formula, which fires fifteen times and locates the defect in the object. **Several listed pairs are things the text asserts in its own voice.** Remedy is **refuge, *"without efforts"***; ch 428 then negates every predicate, including double negations

concepts.title: Every Narrator Is Compromised
concepts.description: three disclosures, none ever used: the transmission chain made of people ch 313 says do not know Śiva; Vyāsa named among the deluded four sentences after asking; and **Sanatkumāra turned into a camel by Nandi for pride and installed as a teacher by Śiva's own instruction** — ⚑ **the office is the punishment completed.** ⛑ Withdraws a standing check closed as negative on **four correct answers to a question one degree off** — the sweep hunted a narrator disqualified inside his own Saṃhitā. `[n=2 SUGGESTIVE]` → `[n≥3 PATTERN]`

concepts.title: The Hells That Fit the Crime
concepts.description: the organ-correspondence rule **stated twice in general form** and then instanced nine times. ⚑ **Four of the nine fall on organs of *perception*, and one punishes a man for *hearing* criticism somebody else spoke** — the rule extended from doing to perceiving and from agency to presence, unannounced. Two doors, a courtesy reception, **Vasiṣṭha running the accounts**, and a jurisdiction map that never mentions the amnesty

concepts.title: Nothing in the Body Is Clean
concepts.description: the disgust-meditation as a **stock list in market measures**, fourteen line-items in kuḍavas, ādhakas and palas, plus a building-figure with one door and eight windows that resolves cleanly on note 1294. **Every enumeration checks.** And the chapters' own summary is not about the body: *"There is supreme grief in a sense of ownership"* — ⚑ **the disgust is the method and valuation is the instrument**

concepts.title: The Eight Forms and the Argument Against Harm
concepts.description: the volume **derives** an ethic: eight mūrtis covering everything including *kṣetrajña*, *"Therefore, the universe has Shiva in its atman"*, the root-and-branch analogy, and the inversion — *"if a person acts so as to **constrain** any embodied being, this is the same as harming his eight forms."* ⚑ **A conclusion nothing downstream uses**, in a volume that licenses brahmanicide in battle, prescribes flesh and fish for a cult, and carries a martyrdom doctrine. Also delivers complete the two schemas Volume 2 delivered broken

concepts.title: Two Boats, Two Rocks
concepts.description: the mutual simile (*"two rocks cannot carry each other across"*), the defect propagating exactly (*"emancipation will also be in name"*), a **specification**, a selection test, and — found nowhere else in three volumes — a **warranty**: *"If no bliss or enlightenment is experienced even after a year, the shishya **must** seek refuge with another guru"*, measured by the disciple's own experience, with a courtesy clause. ⚑⚑ **Beside total obedience on pain of Rourava hell, in one passage**

concepts.title: The Siddhi Cascade
concepts.description: eight tiers at 8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64, eight new items each, **every carry-forward written out**, in a text with no numerals. **The hardest counting task in the corpus and the one it gets right** — ⚑ which is what makes the six announce/deliver failures evidential rather than noise. And the sixty-four powers are framed as things that *"must be contended with"*, dismissed as *"only a small part"*, and given an **evidential** function: *"Since I have seen this, moksha is **also** possible"*

concepts.title: The Yogi's Limbs and Impediments
concepts.description: ten impediments each defined (including ailments from bodily imbalance and *"doubt about the place… should it be this or that?"*), six *upasargas* each defined and five of them sensory upgrades filed as obstacles, **the corpus's only capacity-management rule** (*"A person who is tired of japa, must perform dhyana"*), a mātrā defined by snapping the fingers, prāṇāyāma overdose described clinically, and samādhi as **the exact inverse of the six upasargas**

concepts.title: The Once-Glossed Layer
concepts.description: **116 glossed technical terms, 111 appearing exactly once.** Six carry weight: ***puryaṣṭaka*** with its eight components never enumerated in a text that enumerates everything; ***parivetta/parivitti***; ***nāḍīsandhāna***; ***brahmakūrca***; ***brahmaśilā***; and the ***avabhṛtha***, where **a goddess is instructed to become a river so the audience can bathe at the end of the Purāṇa.** ⚑ Four of the six are invisible to both sweeps and reading — **it takes a count to see that a word never came back**

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 3 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §5I episodes and worked examples, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Guru's Cow
concepts.description: **four controlled cases of one offence in six chapters, with intention the only variable, and the ordering inverts.** Nṛga's honest error → a lizard; Pṛṣadhra's mistaken bull, with the guru **finding the sin *"inadvertent and not voluntary"* and demoting him out of his varṇa anyway**; Triśaṅku's deliberate slaughter → cursed by one brahmana and given a kingdom by another *"While devas and Vasishtha looked on"*; the seven boys' premeditated killing → **punished as cruelty and credited as a good deed in one chapter by one narrator.** Complicates rather than confirms `the-tirtha-launders-anything`: **indifference to intention and inversion of it are indistinguishable in any single case and unmistakable across four**

concepts.title: The Corpus of the Disqualified
concepts.description: **133 litany instances whose exemplars are demons, three courtesans, a caṇḍālī, two hunters, a declared adulterer, a tiger, a man who died as a dog and two people who changed sex** — against access rules that exclude all of them. The two halves touch once, in **endnote 1381: *"Having been a woman earlier, Sudyumna was not entitled to a kingdom."*** Four inclusive statements against four restrictive ones, both absolute, plus a **third scheme** in which śūdras receive padodaka instead of the rite

concepts.title: One Story, Two Gods
concepts.description: the **Kena yakṣa episode told twice with the deity swapped**, Devī in the Umā and Śiva in the Vāyavīya, on a scripted sweep confirming the motif appears in exactly two places. ⚑ **The disclosure travels with the Śaiva telling** — *"I have heard about them from the Upanishads"* at ch 424, nothing at ch 362 — extending the three-level import table to the same import at two levels inside one volume. **The annexation is at the seam:** inside the story Devī never names the yakṣa

concepts.title: Sudyumna, Twice
concepts.description: born male and **cursed** (308) against born female and **granted** manhood as a reward (350); opposite agent, valence and ending. **Endnote 1379 supplies the contradicted version as *"the standard story"*, attached to the chapter that contradicts it**, and supplies a motive the body never gives. Carries Ilā's honoured refusal — the third counter-instance to the routed-around pattern and the only one whose speaker is not a goddess in power

concepts.title: What the Demon Knew
concepts.description: **the volume's most accurate theology is the villain's**, four claims all independently confirmed elsewhere, and he attacks because *"how will I show my face?"* **Kauśikī states the mechanism as a law in the next line.** Sixth instance of the corpus forecast-spine and the only one with full reasoning, so it supplies the missing term — **shame rather than orders.** Sharpens *the demons are the better devotees* into *the better epistemologists*, with no survival value either way

concepts.title: The Goddess Assembled
concepts.description: the demon has **consolidated every divine office** and the gods' remedy is to consolidate themselves: a body assembled part by part, then a **second** operation in which each god hands over his signature emblem. ⚑ **An inventory reading makes that paragraph a complete iconographic disarmament of the pantheon.** And *"Kubera gave her a vessel filled with liquor"* is **standard issue** in a volume listing drinking among the five great sins — with her cult separately prescribed liquor, flesh and fish

concepts.title: The Lineage That Swallowed the Śākyas
concepts.description: Śākya and Śuddhodana filed in the solar dynasty with the son absent. **The word *"Buddha"* occurs exactly once in the volume, in endnote 2053, noting that a daśāvatāra list runs to nine.** Two omissions at two levels, against Volume 2's opposite strategy of inclusion-as-subordination. ⛔ The text's handling, never history

concepts.title: Kill Us Where the Earth Is Not Flooded
concepts.description: **the boon-economy running backwards**, with the text supplying the connective: the demons offer the boon *because* they have been deluded into it, and the god's request is permission to kill them. Their clause is well drafted and specifies nowhere; **he places them on his thighs.** ⚑ The same literal-compliance mechanism runs ten chapters earlier as a **rescue** — so **the letter is decisive rather than fatal, and the drafter never controls the resolution**

concepts.title: Two Kauśikīs
concepts.description: *"emerged from the sheaths in the body"* against *"cast aside her outer skin"*; independent against commissioned; and the second produces Kālī as well. ⚑ **The Vāyavīya tells its version twice and agrees with itself** — two coherent traditions rather than scatter — **and ch 412 declines to re-narrate a battle *"since this has been narrated elsewhere"* in the same chapter that supplies an incompatible origin**

concepts.title: The Courtship That Was an Inventory
concepts.description: a proposal in the vocabulary of acquisition: an itemised scouting report closing on *"all the women who are jewels have become jewels in your inner quarters"*, an offer ranking her against a portfolio taken from gods, and an interchangeable holder. ⚑⚑ **She wins with the incommensurability argument Menā and Satyavatī both lost with** — the corpus's control case, and the reason the women's-positions finding can now name its variable

concepts.title: Dhundhu, Who Breathes Once a Year
concepts.description: a buried danava whose **annual exhalation** shakes the mountains, killed by excavation at the cost of **ninety-seven of a hundred sons in a subordinate clause**, with the kill routed entirely through **Viṣṇu's** energy. The killer's name is announced **three times before the deed**, once from the firmament — the volume's only prospective damage-name

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 3 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §5B the structural spine, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: Only What a Character Asks
concepts.description: **the build's capstone.** Four dialogic detection sites in 160 chapters, every one resolved competently with a real distinction; against a dozen unnoticed doublets, **none of which has an interlocutor.** The text owns **seven** mechanisms for handling its own inconsistency — kalpa-variance stated as a general hermeneutic, a doxography of ~30 contradictory positions blamed on the sages, dialogic detection, a mantra carve-out, ritual exhaustion, purgation inside liberation, back-reference-and-decline — **uses all seven correctly and applies none of them where it matters**, and reconciles its central desert tension five separate ways in five chapters with none referencing another. ⚑ **Detection is entirely dialogic; a listener sees only as far back as the conversation he is in.** ⛔ Marked throughout as the build's synthesis, not a claim the text makes. Withdraws this build's own "never in the same sentence" formulation, which ch 435 falsifies

concepts.title: Named Circularity, Unnoticed Contradiction
concepts.description: six announced loops, **four of them the premise of an argument**: Devī deriving in three steps that Brahmā is her son, father-in-law and grandfather and using it to refuse him standing; devas and ancestors *"successively fathers and sons of each other"* as a settlement; the guru-succession closing on itself with *"therefore, he is the first guru."* **Which excludes the easy defence** — a text that stops to enumerate a three-step kinship loop is not indifferent to structure, so the silence on the doublets is absence of view rather than tolerance. Ch 344 runs both behaviours in one exchange. Carries two further self-references: the sūtas born from Pṛthu inside Suta's own narration, and two authors for this Purāṇa thirty chapters apart

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 3 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §5A the edition, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Apparatus Is the Translator's
concepts.description: a complete census of 2,124 endnotes finds **roughly twenty-three disclosed editorial acts**: fourteen located substitutions including two divine names and aksharas silently repaired inside a mantra, five unlocated liberties (one covering a whole chapter), four structural impositions. **Every one moves the text toward the customary, the consensual, the internally consistent or the natural-sounding — and nobody states it as a policy.** The apparatus is a second voice on doctrine too: two of the corpus's five tattva counts are the translator's, and the Introduction's thirty-six appears nowhere in 160 chapters. Occasionally wrong where the text is right (note 1708's "puzzling" 38 is derived thirteen chapters earlier and used eight times)

concepts.title: The Saṃhitā That Grew
concepts.description: the text publishes its own shloka budget. The original twelve sum to **exactly 100,000**; the abridged seven come within **0.6%** of the printed text overall — but **Umā runs +45.6% and Vidyeśvara −23.0% while the other five sit still.** Scale right, distribution wrong. And Umā is, on the wholly independent frame-flag instrument, the only section carrying demonstrably imported material. **Expansion by absorption in one Saṃhitā; compositional independence between the other two.** Carries a new find: Volume 1 prints the same table with two figures halved, summing to 95,500 while asserting 100,000

concepts.title: The Kailāsa Is a Different Book
concepts.description: twenty-three chapters that are a tantric ritual manual bound into a Purāṇa, with **four independent markers separating them from the Saṃhitā printed next**: 26 tattvas against ~50 *in the same rite with the same spoken formula*; five Praṇava components against four, stated twice on each side (composition, not corruption); Devanāgarī breaking through the edition's transliteration policy where the argument is about letters; and the **Śiva Sūtras cited by number and expounded**. Against which the two agree exactly on burial procedure — independent doctrine, shared practice

concepts.title: Two Numbering Systems That Are Not Unique
concepts.description: the citation-integrity page. **362 names two chapters, 388 names two (across a Saṃhitā boundary), 365 names none**, and endnote numbers restart per section so *"note 12"* is two notes. Both hazards are the translator's own apparatus and **neither is stated anywhere in 2,124 notes.** The Saṃhitā-internal numbering is exact throughout, so the remedy is a citation form: `388-8.1(1)`, never "ch 388," and every endnote with its line reference

concepts.title: The Devotees Who Exist Only in the Endnotes
concepts.description: closes Volume 2's standing check on the five never-narrated devotees: **three zero hits, two recurrences inside another litany.** Asked for the missing stories the apparatus fails twice over — **note 1857 reads, in full, "Narrated in Volume II, Chapter 195-3.5(25)," which is the litany**, and note 1143 supplies a whole story the Purāṇa nowhere contains, unmarked as external. Generates the endnote-provenance rule: **commenting on this text, importing from the tradition, recording an emendation, or hedging — four acts, one typeface, and 48 notes hedge**

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 2 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §8D doctrine & practice, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Pāśupata Charter
concepts.description: a sect's warrant prophesied by the god before the yugas: twenty-eight Vyāsas, four disciples each, **announced at 112 and delivered at 108 — the seventh teacher's four are missing and no note says so** *(corrected 2026-08-11; Volume 3 enumerates the same lineage at 106 and diagnoses a lost shloka)* — ending at Lakuli and a visitable address in Vadodara district. Paired with ch 179, where the paśu condition and its fifteen-year release are issued in one speech, so the problem's reach is calibrated to the cure's. Also separates the term's three senses — vow, weapon, yoga — which the volume never distinguishes

concepts.title: The Five Faces and the Eight Forms
concepts.description: two schemas announced complete and expounded short: Rudra named among the eight and never explained, wind unassigned, a ninth item called the eighth; and taste assigned to Aghora where the scheme gives Aghora the eyes. **Endnotes 716 and 717 patch the gap without saying so, while 719 flags only the smallest of the three problems** — the note layer read as repair, again

concepts.title: The Twelve Jyotirliṅgas
concepts.description: the verse precedes the stories and the stories follow its order twelve for twelve, while a name drifts three ways and two addresses go permanently vague. **Sequence is the durable carrier; wording is not.** Carries the ch 272 tension between an infinite unlistable set of liṅgas and a canonical twelve, four sentences apart

concepts.title: The Liṅga Gazetteer
concepts.description: sixty-six names in one paragraph, six repeated inside it, four jyotirliṅgas demoted to the residual category, a four-direction survey delivered in four incompatible formats, and rewards generated from the names by pun. The story-traces all point back into the volume's own narrated material — **the compiler was indexing his contents, not surveying a countryside**

concepts.title: The Practice Layer
concepts.description: a complete practice that is never collected, transmitted entirely by case. Two explicitly marked tiers, with the highest restriction running **inside the pantheon** (mṛtasañjīvanī kept from Viṣṇu and Brahmā). The aghorāstra made from bhasma by recitation collapses mantra-layer and astra-layer into one system. States its delta against the vault's existing mantra pages rather than duplicating them

concepts.title: Mleccha, Five Ways
concepts.description: **the plan said three; the sweep returns five**, all incompatible, none acknowledging another, and every one of the word's four occurrences sits at a structural joint. Includes ch 269, where the outsider-status is Śiva's own costume and the hero's birth-status reasoning is staged as an error without a word of comment. Reported throughout as the text's classification, never as description

concepts.title: The Indemnity Clause Runs Hot
concepts.description: sixteen deployments of *following the customary practices of the world*, **none of them covering a wrongdoing**. It covers the god having a psychology, which makes it a theological shim rather than a moral indemnity — and cleanly separate from the liability rule the plan had filed it with. Clusters six times across the Gaṇeśa episode and three times in ch 194, which makes it a measurable stress gauge on the doctrine

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 2 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §8C method pages, complete (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Four Doublets and the Four Disclosures
concepts.description: four stories told twice with no acknowledgement (152/154, 183/259, 216/241, 179/253 weaker), against three disclosure mechanisms the volume deploys five times. The finding is not that a compilation repeats itself but that **the norm existed, was in active use, and did not reach the seams** — ch 259 goes further and calls its retelling *original*. Also documents the annotation layer's structural limit: every note works locally and none reaches across chapters, which is why a careful annotator glossed *Jīva* twice without connecting the two

concepts.title: The One Thing the Lens Found
concepts.description: the build's honest method record. The pre-specified frame lens ran 304 chapters for one contested hit, with a strong counter-reading fourteen chapters away; the four unplanned instruments produced everything substantive. The transferable rule: **working instruments measure features the author was not choosing**, because chosen features come out arguable rather than wrong. Carries the failure modes and the 7/7 versus 0/3 diagnostic

concepts.title: The Register Seam at Andhaka
concepts.description: endnote 501 on the ch 214 heading, plus two survivals in the English and a countable spike in repair-annotation density. Filed as **corroboration, not discovery** — the translator raised it first, and blurring the two would inflate the build's record. Zero handshakes, stated

concepts.title: The Formula Count
concepts.description: seven headline formulas re-counted independently over 165,512 words, with chapter-level distribution showing spread rather than clumping. Two classic signatures plus a plot slot, corroborated by a wording-independent structural instrument. The claim is deliberately capped at formulaic composition — and the page notes that high formula density makes voice-based authorship detection on this corpus **harder**, which sits in real tension with the Andhaka seam

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 2 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — §8A continues (2026-08-11)

concepts.title: The Tīrtha Launders Anything
concepts.description: the discharge instrument reads acts and never intentions: a premeditated, pre-costed murder at ch 277 clears as cleanly as a vrata performed by accident at ch 280. **Corrects the plan's framing** — ch 238 and ch 281 both show generic tīrtha-bathing failing explicitly, so the claim holds on the sin axis and fails on the place axis; what launders is a named jurisdiction, and the advertised failures elsewhere are part of the pitch. Set against ch 260's itemised four-debt karmic audit, delivered by Śiva in person, with the contradiction preserved and no reconciling passage in the range read. Also carries brahma-hatyā as a speaking devotee with her own soteriology, expelled by a border rather than dissolved

concepts.title: Closure Without Refutation
concepts.description: five arguments, none answered, `[n=5 PATTERN]` with every instance re-read in sequence. Four instruments produce closure without engaging content: charge the speech to the speaker (159), move the category (176), relocate the agency (205), invoke a prior obligation (296) — plus the manufactured doctrine at 175 that nobody bothered to rebut. None of the four requires knowing whether the argument was good, which is why the volume can print its own accurate charge sheet against Viṣṇu and Indra and leave it standing. The exact negative complement to what-makes-an-argument-win. ⚑ **Volume 3 adds a fifth and sixth instrument, both used on women and both reaching backwards** — delete the ground the objection stands on (358-6(44), Satyavatī transformed mid-refusal) and reattribute the grievance to the aggrieved party as strategy (414-8.1(27), *"you pretended to be angry with me"*) — **plus three counter-instances**, and ch 413-8.1(26) answers the page's own open question against it: an objection met on its content, conceded, and reversed by the opponent. A negative recorded over one volume did not survive the next

concepts.title: The Share-Grievance Migrates
concepts.description: the Dakṣa catastrophe told a third time, collated against Volume 1's file. Vol 1's Satī names the withheld share; **Vol 3's argues her own precedence and never mentions it, and the share-argument reappears two chapters later as Vīrabhadra's legal demand** — *"Give us our shares. If no share has been planned for us in this sacrifice, tell us the reason for that"* — **which is answered on the merits where hers was answered by ranking her sisters' husbands.** Second instance at 349-6(35), where Saṃjñā's objection is granted after her substitute states it; `[n=2 SUGGESTIVE]`. Carries the unflagged **60,000 vs 8,000 gaṇas** discrepancy across volumes, Nandi-as-mount against Nandi-as-escort, and Satī's own curse, which is fulfilled where Volume 1's five forecasts altered nothing

concepts.title: Texts Are Objects; Speech Fails
concepts.description: the four Vedas expound the liṅgam in their own voices and *"those two felt that this was a dream and still did not comprehend"* — then *"everything spoken by the Vedas was **written down on the lingam**. Seeing that this was written down on the lingam, they were placated."* **Same words, same authority, same two listeners; failing as speech and landing as inscription**, in a text whose translator opens by noting that writing came later. Three failure modes — **not believed** (457), **not heeded** (407, the mantras cited as proof by the party they rule against, then departing), **not retained** (375, the sages forgetting what they asked for) — against a book handed over with two hands and enthroned at initiation, and Vedas stolen and physically returned. Failure `[n≥3 PATTERN]`; the writing remedy is one scene and is called one

concepts.title: Two Hells, Two Shadows, Two Tattva Counts
concepts.description: hells **below** the nether regions at 322 and *"**above** the nether regions"* at 330; a headless shadow meaning death in a month at 339 and aphasia in six at 342, same speaker, one unbroken conversation; and the Virajā oblation performed in two Saṃhitās with **the same spoken sentence**, purifying 26 tattvas *"ending with Purusha"* in one and ~50 running past him in the other. Praṇava settles the species — **five components in the Kailāsa stated twice, four in the Vāyavīya stated twice** — since corruption scatters and this produces two coherent positions. ⭐ Plus the unaided find: **ch 374 and ch 419 are ~90% the same paragraph**, and inside it *"the **five** kinds of jnana"* against *"the **ten**"*, each glossed to fit its own number by an editor whose neighbouring notes are word-identical 273 apart

concepts.title: Announced and Delivered
concepts.description: **seven announce/deliver gaps, two flagged**: four kinds of mukti and a fifth named; *"among these four"* naming a fifth vrata; ten sons and nine listed; eighteen Purāṇas rolled and seventeen described with *"the account of Matsya in Matsya and Matsya is described in Matsya"* in Kūrma's slot; fourteen kinds of vidya called eighteen one sentence later. ⭐ The one the translator chased resolved into damage — *"There should be 112 names for shishyas, but we only have 106, **suggesting one shloka is missing from the text**."* And the negative control is what makes it evidence: an **eight-tier siddhi cascade checking at every rung**

concepts.title: Three Sāmbas
concepts.description: one episode told 108 chapters and two Saṃhitās apart, disagreeing on place, initiation, interval, boon count and **who the child is**. ⚚ **The finding is referential rather than stylistic**: the Vāyavīya version opens *"went and met **Dhoumya's elder brother** and performed **Pashupata vrata**… **We have heard this earlier**"* — and Dhaumya occurs five times in the volume, **all five in the Vāyavīya**, while *Pāśupata* does not occur in the Umā telling at all. **It cross-references itself correctly and does not know the other version exists.** Endnote 1918 then supplies a third identity, unhedged

concepts.title: The Chakra, Given Twice
concepts.description: the Sudarśana awarded twice in three chapters, and **every difference removes Viṣṇu's initiative**: he searches the earth at 305 and shrugs at 307, his eye-offering completes in one and is interrupted in the other, he petitions in one and is pre-empted in the other. ⚚⚚ **And the litany between them hands off with *"After this, Shambhu engaged in an extremely wonderful pastime"*** — a doublet introduced as a continuation, where detection fires only when a listener objects and a transition sentence has no listener. The second telling carries the origin the corpus had been missing: *"had originated from his own feet"*

concepts.title: The Strata This Purāṇa Carries
concepts.description: **eight things in a Purāṇa that are not Purāṇic**, reported and deliberately not dated: a 13×13 maṇḍala with bīja mantras given by alphabetic position; khecarī and kākī described by method and never named; a recursive Paśu/Pāśa/Pati catechism with the five kañcukas; dīkṣā as physiology (*"the consciousness, **which is like a blue dot**"*); a Śākta chain; the devayāna/pitṛyāna pair personified into ten deities and feminised, absorbed with no attribution; and a mātrā defined by a finger-snap. ⚚⚚ **And one citation worth more than the rest combined** — *"There is a **Shivasutra** that states, '**chaitanyamatma**'… The second Shivasutra states, '**jnanam bandhadh**'"*, with the apparatus supplying *"revealed to Vasugupta"*

concepts.title: Who May Be Initiated
concepts.description: **three incompatible answers, none acknowledging the others**: *"irrespective of varna or ashrama, women, children, male servants, female servants"* and *"regardless of whether he is **antyaja**"*, against *"men are divided into **three varnas**"*, against a derivative scheme where *"**On their own, women do not possess the rights**… a woman without a husband must seek the son's permission."* Śūdras are not barred but **substituted** — *"Sins can be cleansed by offering **padodaka**"* — and the qualifying test is stated cruelty. ⛑ One inherited attribution withdrawn: **ch 430 contains no varṇa term at all**

concepts.title: Dīkṣā Is a Varṇa Promotion
concepts.description: ch 335 prices varṇa mobility in *"thousands of births"* both ways; ch 438 runs the same rungs in one ceremony, upward only, and past the top: *"**raised up to the status of a kshatriya and then… a brahmana**… then **raised up to the status of Rudra**."* **Three things vanish in the compression** — the downward direction, the disciple's own qualifying practice, and the bottom rung, since the ladder starts at vaiśya. **A mechanism that dissolves rank does not need a rank requirement**, and the incumbent is told he can skip the intermediate steps. Priced in *"wealth, jewels, fields, homes… vehicles, beds and seats"*

concepts.title: The Praṇava Diagram
concepts.description: **the liṅgam as a chart**: each Veda *"established itself in ten aspects"*, delivering guṇa, deity, function, tattva, kalā, brahman-face and **a physical height on the stone**, each stated by the Veda in the first person. The scheme manifests **during a precedence quarrel and gives the two quarrellers the two lowest positions**, deriving *"Shiva is the supreme cause"* from a mapping rather than asserting it. ⛑ **And the fourth column will not count** — *"it is impossible to precisely count which ten are meant"* — with two further worlds stacked above the scheme's own terminus

concepts.title: The Mendicant's Burial
concepts.description: *"**There are no burning rites for mendicants who are emancipated**… their bodies are buried."* A ditch *"as long as a staff"*, the body *"**in a posture of yoga and facing the east**"*, and *"**a coconut will be used to splinter the skull into four parts**."* **Kapāla-kriyā transposed rather than dropped** — and the Vāyavīya, which disagrees with the Kailāsa on every technical question tested, prescribes the same disposal in its own vocabulary (*"not… the way they are undertaken for a **Pashu**"*). **Divergent doctrine over a shared institutional floor**

concepts.title: Criticising Śiva Outranks Homicide
concepts.description: **six sectarian sins with *"infinite consequences"* attached**, then the classical five printed accurately and **without the qualifier**, with a roster between them *"equal in impact to an act of criticizing Shiva"* that includes *"**wilfully sleeping in a spot that has not been cleaned**."* **The classical five require an act; the six and their roster are largely failures to act**, which makes breach the default state. And wounding speech is itself brahmanicide, so both catalogues are substantially a speech code

concepts.title: Objections That Block Are Engineered Around; the One That Prices Is Paid
concepts.description: four objections, four machines. Birth **deferred**; her body's premise **deleted** (*"in an instant, **she was transformed into Yojanagandha**"*); the daytime prohibition **satisfied rather than overruled** (*"he immediately **constructed a mist**"*); and the pregnancy objection, which only prices the act, **paid in a five-clause settlement.** ⚚⚚ **The sorting tracks the responder's costs, not the claim** — and her name is a clause in the contract

concepts.title: The Inventory of What You Are Giving Away
concepts.description: Vyāsa asks for the one gift that covers all gifts, is told *"**he must donate the universe**"*, and immediately asks *"**Please tell me about the size and nature of the universe**"* — **and seven chapters of cosmography follow.** **The geography is a schedule of the thing being handed over**, with Pātāla given floors of gold and a testimonial that it beats heaven. And the donor owns none of it while the return is *"lordship of the seven worlds"* — so what is scheduled is the extent of a renunciation

concepts.title: Heterodoxy as a Manufactured Weapon
concepts.description: **the whole page reports the text's polemic and describes no living tradition.** The ch 174 commissioning brief read as a specification — length, doctrine, omissions, language, deployment area, activation date — with advance indemnity, a planted convert, and operatives immunised against their own product. The doctrine is never refuted anywhere in ch 175–189, so the volume's two most humane sentences stand unopposed inside the chapter written to bury them. Ch 182 clears the manufacturers and damns the future believers in one speech. Ch 298 runs the instrument backwards on a contemporary sect and is the volume's most datable material. Ch 186 folds the manufactured heresy into Viṣṇu's avatāra list, closing a loop in which no dissent originates outside the pantheon

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 2 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Mechanism pages, §8A opens (2026-08-10)

concepts.title: Whole Narratives Annexed
concepts.description: the episode-level instrument, six instances, five inside twenty chapters. The method is retelling rather than argument, which is why it cannot be rebutted. Three findings the plan did not have: what is taken is always the **moment of rescue** and never doctrine; ch 212–213 is a deliberate counter-case, with Varāha and Nṛsiṃha left intact because their outcome is a killing; and the volume's citation habit is pointed **only inward** — it tracks provenance meticulously within its own material and never once outward. Also notes that the annexations extract no debt, no rite and no follower

concepts.title: The Sudarśana, Worked Eight Ways
concepts.description: **count corrected from seven to eight** by sweep; ch 265 is a distinct operation and ch 244 is a back-reference, not a ninth. The argument is not about provenance, which the operations contradict each other on at no cost, but about **jurisdiction** — the weapon keeps working, keeps being Viṣṇu's, and cannot be used against Śiva's people. Notes that the transfers reach their securest form in recited material (the Puruṣa-sūkta at ch 226, Vāsavānuja at ch 219) where nothing can be contested, and that the sequence opens with Viṣṇu giving the discus away voluntarily

concepts.title: The Refuge-Duty That Binds Everyone
concepts.description: five deployments across four speakers, including one against the god who states it. The rule is unaimable because it triggers on an act rather than on a judgement, and riggable for the same reason. Adds the ch 278 widow, who invokes it from total powerlessness with no merit assessed, and pairs the rule with the liability rule as the corpus's only two automatic principles — one creating an obligation by the weak party's act, one extinguishing it by the strong party's, both operated by the same figure

concepts.title: Damage Becomes Institution
concepts.description: the corpus's signature resolution, across four output formats, with the lunar cycle as its purest case. **Corrects the Phase 1 etiology claim**, which rested on nine sampled instances all selected for being injury-derived; a proper whole-body sweep returns 32 naming instances across 26 chapters, of which roughly eleven are injury-derived, so the claim holds for narrative name-origins and not for naming generally. Also states the boundary — the volume does repair relationships, where somebody repents alive — and that the conversion is almost always requested by the injured party

concepts.title: The Feminine as Something Assumed
concepts.description: five of six new female divine forms have an explicit male author in the sentence introducing them, and each is an access technology rather than an honour. Adds two negatives the count needed: no male form is ever assumed to solve an access problem, and no goddess in the range read creates a male one. Explicitly refuses to average the volume's gender material, and sets the counter-evidence out at length

concepts.title: Worship Me First, or Nothing Counts
concepts.description: precedence as a validity condition rather than a hierarchy, stated five times and enforced once against Śiva. Two findings the plan did not have: every holder is a **doorkeeper**, so the rule is that post transposed into ritual sequence; and ch 284 supplies the volume's only **empirical test** of a ritual claim — a standard with a prior stated meaning that falls early when the vāṭuka is fed first. Also carries the ch 180 narratorial pre-emptive defence as the body-side counterpart to Debroy's note 500

concepts.title: The God in Costume
concepts.description: the count established by sweeping the volume's own test-construction rather than by judgement: fourteen, twelve on the strictest Śiva-only reading, robust either way. The concealment produces uncontestable evidence rather than information, and the disclosure is the payload. Carries the two boundary cases Volume 1 lacked — the subject who dies at ch 257 and the subject never told at ch 283 — and the costume-design finding, that Śiva wears his rival's face precisely when testing exclusivity

concepts.title: The Supreme Dharmas, and Who Says Them
concepts.description: eight incompatible superlative dharma-claims, four of them spoken inside an active deception, and only two sincere. The volume's method for disposing of a claim is to settle its speaker rather than answer it, which is why the humane doctrine it wrote for its own heretic stands unrebutted. An eighth section widens the problem past the liars: Śiva's own ranked absolute at ch 205, the formal adjudication at ch 274–275, and the demons' at ch 218 collide with each other too

concepts.title: What Makes an Argument Win
concepts.description: the corrected finding: argument never wins on its content, only when it converts into a citation the opponent has already endorsed. Two outright winners, tagged n equals 2 suggestive, plus a third deployment at ch 298 recorded and deliberately not counted. Carries the ch 304 internal control — the same speaker's moral appeal failing and her citation winning four lines apart — and the corrections to both the Volume 1 record and this build's own earlier draft

concepts.title: The Righteous Demon Problem
concepts.description: five enemies, no charge sheet, and the text's own admiring descriptions of their rule. The resolution is category-work in both directions: reclassify the good ruler out of demon-hood, or reclassify the devout population into mlecchas. Carries ch 205 in full — the messenger's reductio from Śiva's own premise, and Śiva's reply denying and asserting partiality in one speech — plus the four demon speeches that are the volume's best statements of dharma

concepts.title: The Boon That Cannot Be Refused
concepts.description: the boon is not a gift but a procedure for converting an unspecified vulnerability into a documented one, and nobody in the corpus can decline it. Carries ch 301 with the correction that Śiva concedes *before* Pārvatī argues, which removes it from the winning-argument set; the identical Brahmā coaching script at ch 171 and ch 214; and the second output, in which the grant knowingly becomes the enemy's operational capacity

concepts.title: Liability and the Undisclosed Impairment
concepts.description: the rule that decides who pays, and it tracks disclosure rather than causation, rank or kinship. The pre-issued indemnity covers an atrocity; the undisclosed impairment convicts its victim. Arundhatī is the control the text prints and never draws an inference from, and ch 224 is the one fully specified case in which nobody is billed. States its own limits: the indemnity protects operatives, never targets, and the corpus never applies the test to Śiva

concepts.title: The Commission Pattern
concepts.description: Śiva is never quoted issuing the instruction in any of the eight operations against a third party; all five attributions to him are narratorial, and the one quoted commission he does give (ch 224) is an order for his own incapacitation, and the three spoken commissions belong to Pārvatī and the devas. The agent devises the method in every narratorial case. Ch 176 has the two registers openly disagreeing and the page preserves it

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 2 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Episode pages, first cluster (2026-08-10)

concepts.title: Kumāra, and the Son Who Left
concepts.description: a conception routed through five custodians who each call themselves incapable, a twelve-witness deposition that confesses everything and punishes nobody, and a son who states he contains no portion of his mother; the estrangement is never repaired, it is timetabled

concepts.title: Gaṇeśa: Made, Beheaded, and Promoted
concepts.description: created to one specification ("he must not deviate the least bit from my instructions") and killed for meeting it; the war is fought to prevent a rumour, the kill is done by deceit on the god's own stated policy, and universal precedence is the ransom price

concepts.title: Tripura, the Hardest Case
concepts.description: three cities of Śiva-worshippers with a Rudra temple in every house, destroyed by a corruption the text will not attribute to a single author; Śiva names Viṣṇu and Nārada, Brahmā names Śiva, and the annihilation contradicts itself in three consecutive sentences

concepts.title: The Two Wives Who Were the Weak Point
concepts.description: two demon kings whose invulnerability is lodged in another person's fidelity, and the two operations that void it; the goddess names wifely fidelity the highest dharma on earth in the sentence ordering its destruction, and Tulasī's unanswered question states the whole problem. **Carries the `[FALSIFIED]` obituary for the supposed ch 196/211 tulasī origin-doublet**, overturned here on a sequential re-read

concepts.title: The Liṅga That Had to Be Caught
concepts.description: the volume's own origin for the liṅga-in-yoni, stated without allegory as a containment vessel; the corpus's one undisclosed disguise, the provoked-then-billed variant of the disabled-then-billed machine, and the only component in existence *capable* of holding it. Records the Dārukavana name-collision with ch 300 as a collision and not a doublet

concepts.title: Nine Heads for a Trick
concepts.description: the most expensive worship in either volume answered with a disclosed condition the granter then breaks himself; Nārada commissioned by the devas, flattering the unwitnessed cost; the curse triggered by Pārvatī's sarcasm rather than by the offence; and an operation that ends with its target unopposable. Carries the ch 271 précis that kept the word *deceit*

concepts.title: The Two Gautama Accounts
concepts.description: the volume's control case on disclosure: the listeners raise the repetition, Sūta names kalpa-variance and narrates the variant in full, which is what makes the non-use of the same machinery on ch 216/241 and ch 183/259 a finding rather than an excuse. The two endings are consequences, not temperaments — Gaṇeśa performs the frame-up in version one, the brahmanas manufacture it themselves in version two. The ch 298 curse is carried as the text's polemic and as dating evidence, never as description

concepts.title: Kāśī Promises Everything and Takes It Back
concepts.description: the city made before the world because austerity had nowhere to stand, and the widest offer in the corpus — caste, gender, ritual purity, species, knowledge, worship and devotion all removed as conditions — retracted a page later in the same speech by one speaker. The three-karma taxonomy is real doctrine laid beside an incompatible promise rather than reconciling it, and the access condition forecloses the only evidence that could count against the offer

concepts.title: The Śarabha and the Hide
concepts.description: the volume's largest doublet: Nṛsiṃha's unstoppable rage is resolved twice, incompatibly, twenty-five chapters apart, off the same three-element setup, and neither account is flagged. Carries the qualification that endnote 779 narrows the death-claim to the form, and the competing frame-difference reading. Then the absorption machine at its extreme — flayed, worn, and canonised in one chapter, with the victim's consent obtained mid-beating

concepts.title: The Vedas Testified and Were Overruled
concepts.description: the volume's second evidentiary proceeding, and the pair to ch 154's. Both disputants pre-commit to accept the Vedas' finding, all four testify for Rudra, Praṇava assumes a body to answer their objection — and they reject it by impugning the witnesses and substituting a criterion about Śiva's appearance. What produces belief is the beheading. The sin that follows is generated by Śiva afterwards as a demonstration, and Viṣṇu's objection that it cannot apply to Śiva at all is printed and left unanswered

concepts.title: Ardhanārī, and the Origin of Satī
concepts.description: Brahmā cannot create through couples because no women had emerged from Īśāna's lineage; Śiva assumes the half-woman form in order to be split, and Śivā is detached, grants the capacity, and is reabsorbed at the chapter's end. The rider attached to the favour — become the daughter of my son, Dakṣa — is the antecedent of Volume 1's central catastrophe, and neither end of the link acknowledges the other

concepts.title: Uṣā, and the Sentence Passed in Advance
concepts.description: the outcome is announced a chapter in advance, in specifics, by the party who causes it; the goddess's own māyā carries the man in and her own attendants carry him back out. The ruling gives two incompatible reasons in one breath. The occasion was Śiva's own stated arousal and nothing attaches to him. Then an ally supplies a prior sin, the victim accepts it, and the grievance never returns — the third of the volume's three commissioned violations, and the one needing no commission at all

concepts.title: The Swallowing of Śukra
concepts.description: Śiva taught the enemy's guru to revive the dead, kept it secret from Viṣṇu and Brahmā, and when it was turned on his own troops could only swallow the man whole; Śukra names the impropriety himself and proceeds on the refuge-duty, the one principle in the volume that binds both sides. Nārāyaṇa's world is itemised among the sights inside Śiva's stomach, as scenery rather than as argument

concepts.title: Andhaka, and the Clause He Wrote Himself
concepts.description: born from Śiva's sweat in a game, given away, and told by Brahmā to accept a means of death; the clause he drafts names nobody, Brahmā ratifies it only after consulting Śiva, and the empty slot had already been filled by Śiva assigning Pārvatī as his foster-mother. Also carries the ch 214 register seam — endnote 501 plus the two English corroborations, kept explicitly separate from it — and **a correction to this build's reading of endnote 511**

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster G-iii (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: Vishnu Tells Brahma He Hates Shiva
concepts.description: the volume's fullest doctrinal statement delivered by Vishnu as a rebuke, naming the motive as hatred and diagnosing the error as treating Rudra as a son; it changes nothing and is metabolised into the pitch one chapter later

concepts.title: Devi Objects and Agrees
concepts.description: she names the delusion, the causation and the target's indifference with complete technical accuracy, and agrees; nobody overrules her, and the objection preserves her omniscience while allowing the plot to run

concepts.title: I Have Been Sent by Brahma
concepts.description: three thousand divine years of austerity on somebody else's grievance, closing with nine words of plain attribution; the person furthest from the injury pays the most

concepts.title: Daksha Curses Narada
concepts.description: the listener of the narration is told to his face how he was cursed, by the man who commissioned the project he obstructed; and he is at both ends of the Khanda's causation

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster G-ii (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: The Twilights Are Her Body
concepts.description: made invisible to walk into a working priesthood's fire, burnt with the offering cakes, conveyed to the sun and divided in two; the evening half feeds the ancestors her presence produced, and three chapters of sandhya regulation never mention it

concepts.title: Sandhya Blames Herself
concepts.description: the only person in the chapter who concludes she has done something wrong is the woman who was looked at, and nobody accuses her; the tradition keeps the confession and builds her sanctity on it

concepts.title: The Woman Who Legislated Puberty
concepts.description: four life-quarters with desire in the third, established in the world; the volume's only ordinance with no escape clause and its only cosmological claim that explains something observable

concepts.title: Arundhati Marries Her Disguised Teacher
concepts.description: Brahma sends one of the four sages who failed, in disguise, so she will not be ashamed; she chooses the disguise as a husband and is reborn to marry the man beneath it

concepts.title: Let Him Become a Eunuch
concepts.description: the bodily defence is the fifth of five boons, after her reputation; the only protection in the volume that requires nothing of the protected person, granted in full and never used

concepts.title: Vasanta From a Breath
concepts.description: spring exhaled as a by-product of planning a seduction, assigned to a person rather than a task, and a structural objection answered four times with resource

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster G-i — **SATI KHANDA OPENS** (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: So As to Confound Hara
concepts.description: the Sati Khanda opens with Brahma confessing that he created Sati to confound Shiva after Shiva laughed at him for desiring his own daughter; Vishnu names it as hatred and Devi as delusion, and both comply

concepts.title: Give Me a Task
concepts.description: six created beings across two Samhitas open their existence with the same request for an assignment; a formula rather than a duplication, and the first finding of its class made without the translator (updated 2026-08-10: the sixth instance, the Maras of ch 61, met the idiom threshold)

concepts.title: Kama Cursed for Doing His Job
concepts.description: commissioned without exemptions, told his powers would work on Brahma himself, and cursed on a charge of insolence after voluntarily withdrawing

concepts.title: The Ancestors Born From Shame-Sweat
concepts.description: the pitris condensed from Brahma's sweat of humiliation and from four named sages who could not restrain themselves; Rati from Daksha's sweat

concepts.title: The Khanda That Summarises Itself
concepts.description: the whole arc told in chapter one and then told again; the volume's only deliberate doubling and therefore the control case for the column of fire and the question block

concepts.title: Rati and the Five Arrows
concepts.description: harshana, rochana, mohana, shoshana, marana: a five-stage progression from pleasure to killing, supplied inside a wedding chapter

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster F-iv-b — **UNIT 3 COMPLETE** (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: Gunanidhi the Thief
concepts.description: the volume's only fully observed household; a mother who lies for years, a father who recites an inventory instead of accusing her, and a living son's funeral rites performed the same afternoon as a remarriage

concepts.title: The Lamp He Tore His Garment For
concepts.description: not a lamp knocked over but a garment torn deliberately for light to steal by; the merit constructed at the trial, and the doctrine that saves him licensing King Dama's beheadings

concepts.title: Starvation Counted as a Fast
concepts.description: hunger credited as fasting and criminal concentration as one-pointedness; a second grace doctrine that credits the wrong intention rather than ignoring intention

concepts.title: Yama's Standing Order
concepts.description: never collect anyone wearing ash, rudraksha or matted hair, even in insolence or deceit; insignia as a jurisdictional boundary rather than a purification

concepts.title: The Glance That Burst an Eye
concepts.description: four verdicts on one look, three agreeing, and the fourth prevailing on standing; the exculpation removes the blame and leaves the injury

concepts.title: The Sages Made From Body Parts
concepts.description: the mind-born sages sourced to eyes, ears, four vital airs, a lap and a shadow; an inconsistent taxonomy read as stratigraphy

concepts.title: The Gana Census
concepts.description: fifty-seven named gana leaders with the arithmetic abandoned mid-clause; enumeration as devotion rather than as accountancy

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster F-iv-a (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: The Creations That Failed
concepts.description: five attempts with the rejects never deleted; the devas judged a failure and humans the success, because a being with nothing lacking cannot be a practitioner

concepts.title: Shiva Refuses to Create
concepts.description: he declines to make beings who suffer and hands the job back with an indemnity granted in advance; the problem of evil distributed rather than resolved

concepts.title: Rudra Originated From My Heart
concepts.description: Shiva does not go to Kailasa; he adopts a form and sends it, and the god everyone worships is the last link in three delegations

concepts.title: The Egg That Had No Consciousness
concepts.description: a complete cosmos found to be insentient, with consciousness supplied by inserting a being who already has it

concepts.title: In a Different Kalpa
concepts.description: the volume's universal contradiction-solvent, deployed exactly once; its tolerance for multiplicity is a field of view rather than a worldview

concepts.title: Why a Swan and a Boar
concepts.description: the swan chosen for discrimination and losing it, because a creator cannot generate jnana; the column-of-fire failure as structural rather than moral

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster F-iii-b — **UNIT 3 CLOSES** (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: The Ketaka Still Banned
concepts.description: the Rudra Samhita omits the ketaki crime in ch 39-40 and still enforces its penalty in ch 46; the omission is demonstrably not ignorance, and only the ban travelled while the concession did not

concepts.title: The Gross and the Subtle Lingam
concepts.description: the physical lingam demoted to a support for those who cannot manage without one, and a total exemption from all rules granted on self-assessment

concepts.title: The Flowers Weighed on a Scale
concepts.description: the volume's two numerical grammars fuse; matched offerings acquire counts, weights and thresholds, and become comparable

concepts.title: The Prices That Do Not Match
concepts.description: every overlapping price between ch 28 and ch 46 rises, none falls; a directional ratchet, and evidence that most of the volume's large numbers are rhetoric

concepts.title: The Lingams Vishvakarma Made
concepts.description: nineteen gods issued lingams according to entitlements, from ruby to flour, with no god objecting; brahmanas get earth, which the yuga sequence makes the highest allocation

concepts.title: The Ladder From Satsang to Brahman
concepts.description: devotion given a linear origin outside itself, terminating at association with the virtuous; six rungs and no quantities anywhere

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster F-iii-a (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: Two Manuals That Do Not Agree
concepts.description: north against south, eight rinses against sixteen, and the two Rudra chapters disagreeing with each other; a procedural contradiction no argument from style can dissolve

concepts.title: The Second Morning Protocol
concepts.description: three mornings, identical in sequence and almost nowhere else; the invariant was carried in bodies and the variable was held only by the manuscript

concepts.title: I Do Whatever You Engage Me In
concepts.description: the prescribed first utterance of the day is a confession of having no moral agency; the volume's agency doctrine installed as liturgy rather than argued as narrative

concepts.title: Worship by Varna, Again
concepts.description: earth-counts and twig-lengths graded by birth in an act nobody can witness; women assigned shudra practice in a subordinate clause

concepts.title: Asked and Answered Before
concepts.description: two incompatible transmission chains four sentences apart, and a god irritated at being asked what was already answered

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster F-ii (2026-08-09)

concepts.title: The Darkness That Cannot Be Pierced With a Needle
concepts.description: mahāpralaya as a demolition in order, then a needle that slips through gaps: the dark has no weave. Read the negations backwards and what survives is the thesis

concepts.title: The Brahman Decides to Have a Second
concepts.description: *"after some time, it decided to have a second"* — a timing and a deciding the preceding page has just abolished, with wanting company as first cause; then the original vanishes

concepts.title: Kashi Exists Before Creation
concepts.description: the city built before the universe and exempted from dissolution in a subordinate clause: *Avimukta*, the never-forsaken. The one geography with no escape clause attached

concepts.title: Viṣṇu Created to Bear the Burden
concepts.description: the cosmos gets a manager so a couple can enjoy Ānandavana undisturbed; the delegate arrives blank and must ask for a name and a task

concepts.title: The Water That Came Out of Viṣṇu
concepts.description: the cosmic ocean is sweat, declared sin-destroying in the next clause; the twenty-four tattvas assemble while he sleeps on it

concepts.title: Brahmā Climbs the Stalk for Two Hundred Years
concepts.description: sound reasoning applied to a thing with no ends; what works is stopping. The confusion was installed by his father's māyā

concepts.title: The Second Column of Fire
concepts.description: the founding myth retold by the man it convicts, with the ketakī, the lie, Bhairava and the stripping of worship all absent, and nothing anywhere acknowledging the doubling

concepts.title: AUM Seen Rather Than Heard
concepts.description: announced as a *nāda* and described entirely in positions; a sound cannot be dwelt in and a layout can. Then the alphabet becomes the god's body

concepts.title: The Golden Egg Struck by Īśvara
concepts.description: it does not hatch, it is struck; a rival cosmogony absorbed by keeping the image intact and replacing everything holding it up

concepts.title: There Is No Difference Between You and Rudra
concepts.description: parity by decree with mutual hell clauses, undone by a Prakṛti clause offered as a secret

Einstein: relativity means body is relative to observer. You seek aliveness, not body; trying to complete self with incomplete matter fails. Cross-Domain: Physics (Gödel/Heisenberg/Einstein principles), Psychology (void as perception, not problem)

concepts.title: Flow vs. Transaction: The Difference Between Having and Participating
concepts.description: Flow: two hours of conversation, no scorekeeper, both fuller. Transaction: I paid last time, you owe me. Moment you count, energy dies. Milk circuit works only if both participate without ownership. Cross-Domain: Economics (flow unmeasurable by transaction), Psychology (secure attachment requires flow not fairness)

concepts.title: The Shamshan Path: Practice in the Cremation Ground
concepts.description: Ascetic lives in cremation ground (nobody's land). Owns nothing → cannot lose anything → cannot be rejected → immune to control systems. Shamshan path refuses even structure of spiritual institutions. Freedom through homelessness and non-belonging. Cross-Domain: History (renunciate traditions), Behavioral-Mechanics (immunity from control)

concepts.title: The Mexican Fisherman Paradox: The Pursuit That Returns You to the Start
concepts.description: Businessman describes wealth-building ending in: rest, fishing, simple meals (the fisherman's present life). Hedonic treadmill: each achievement spikes happiness, baseline returns. Pursuing future fantasy that was present from start. Cross-Domain: Psychology (hedonic treadmill), Behavioral-Mechanics (status systems as perpetual motivation)

concepts.title: Meaninglessness from Fullness vs. Despair Nihilism: The Same Statement, Different Ground
concepts.description: Two people say "nothing matters": one from emptiness (collapse, existential nihilism), one from fullness (release, abundance). Same words, opposite ground. Charvaka nihilism is liberation; Western existential nihilism is despair. Cross-Domain: Psychology (anhedonia vs. equanimity), Behavioral-Mechanics (system resistance)

concepts.title: Pleasure as Compass: What the Body Knows That Culture Teaches You to Ignore
concepts.description: Lion eats meat (instinct knows), human taught not to trust sensation. Pleasure/pain are biological signals, not moral categories. Interoception vs. alexithymia. Practice: listen to what actually sustains you. Cross-Domain: Psychology (interoceptive literacy), Behavioral-Mechanics (control through shame)

concepts.title: Control Through Naming: How Words Fix the Flowing Into Place
concepts.description: Name emotion "anxiety" and it stops flowing, becomes object. Meditation mantras: subtle subjugation through naming. Language inherently reductive; categories kill aliveness. Practice: stay unnamed, unlabeled, in flow. Cross-Domain: Linguistics (Sapir-Whorf), Behavioral-Mechanics (classification as control tool)

concepts.title: Attraction as Aliveness: What You're Actually Lusting For
concepts.description: Two identical bodies: one alive/present, one checked out. Attracted to aliveness, not features. Seduction through presence. Affairs feel alive because flow still present; long-term relationships lose aliveness when ownership begins. Cross-Domain: Psychology (affect synchrony), Physics (uncertainty principle applied to possession)

concepts.title: The Mantra of Recognition: Ma

Cross-Domain: Linguistics (primacy of recognition), Physics (matter as alive/creative)
