concepts.description: liberation = the soul attains Śiva-nature but does not merge or lose individuality; becomes a siddha who can teach

concepts.title: Caryā–Kriyā–Yoga–Jñāna: Siddhānta's Fourfold Path
concepts.description: the tantra structure of conduct, ritual, practice and vision; grace culminates in jñāna

concepts.title: Why Selvalingam Distrusts Bhakti: The Case for Jñāna
concepts.description: bhakti's three dangers (sentimentalism→superstition→weak mind); "can wreck the nerves"; jñāna as safety

concepts.title: Nonsectarian Bhakti & the Objectivity of Mystical Vision
concepts.description: temple-seizing sectarianism critiqued; Brahmananda seeing the Goddess in a Viṣṇu temple → "objectivity to mysticism"

title: The Nāyaṉmār & the Tamil Bhakti Canon (5)

concepts.title: The 63 Nāyaṉmār: Tamil Shaiva Bhakti Saints
concepts.description: the Śiva saints of the medieval Tamil bhakti renaissance; counterpart to the Vaiṣṇava Ālvārs; peak 7th–8th c.

concepts.title: The Four Chief Nāyaṉmār
concepts.description: the lineage premised on four central saints: Sambandar, Appar, Sundarar and Manikkavacakar, and their roles

concepts.title: Manikkavacakar: "Jewel-Speech," the Nāyaṉār Par Excellence
concepts.description: "jewel-speech"; the Tiruvāsakam; debated Buddhists across a curtain; Śiva himself wrote down his song

concepts.title: Sundaramūrti Nāyaṉār: The Bond-Slave Bridegroom
concepts.description: born for the sin-of-lust; Śiva's slavery-document blocks his wedding; sakhya-bhāva; the grain miracle

concepts.title: Tēvāram & Tiruvāsakam: The Tamil Shaiva Hymn Canon
concepts.description: Sundarar's Tēvāram and Manikkavacakar's Tiruvāsakam; sung in temples today; the Tirumuṟai compiled by Nambi Āṇḍār Nambi

concepts.title: The Vātūlanātha Sūtra: Aphorisms of the Intoxicated God
concepts.description: Śiva as Vātūlanātha, the drunk lord; the closing offering "Om Bātula Nāth Arpanamastu"; intoxication as a refined category

concepts.title: Dhatūra: Śiva's Poisonous Hallucinogen
concepts.description: Śiva's "favorite," stronger than acid — and poisonous; people die or lose their minds; carries an explicit death warning, never how-to

concepts.title: Bhāṅg, Blue Lassi & the Gāñjā Babas of Varanasi
concepts.description: ethnography of the chillum and the "blue lassi" code; document-don't-endorse with the author's disclaimer

concepts.title: Siddhi as Gāñjā: The Ramakrishna Double Meaning
concepts.description: "siddhi" means both occult power and ganja-as-offering; the "pass the siddhi around" scene; siddhis demystified as natural

concepts.title: When the Weed Becomes Your Boss: Intoxication vs Svātantrya
concepts.description: transgression is for renouncing purity-rules, not enjoyment; addiction = sovereignty gone; the batch's svātantrya signal

concepts.title: Lakshmanjoo & Madhula Avasthā: The Contagious High
concepts.description: the grocery-store samādhi anecdotes; madhula avasthā as the state of intoxication; the contact-high of nearness to a God-drunk saint

concepts.title: If She Does Not Trust Me, I Will Abandon Her
concepts.description: Śiva's exit clause, set in ch 68 before Satī is asked and never disclosed to her; triggered by a doubt he told her to act on

concepts.title: A Son Who Can Kill What We Cannot
concepts.description: the marriage argued to Śiva as procurement for an unstaffed slot in a list of asuras and their assigned killers

concepts.title: He Answered Before She Could Ask
concepts.description: Satī cannot name her own boon; Śiva cuts in with "be my wife," and her consent is recorded as a silence with a narrator's gloss

concepts.title: The Puns That Carry Doctrine
concepts.description: vara, tata and guru: three flagged double meanings, none adjudicated, each holding up something the tradition treats as settled

concepts.title: He Had Not Told Her About That Either
concepts.description: Śiva withheld the Prayāga quarrel; Satī rides to the sacrifice believing her parents merely forgot her

concepts.title: The Nanda Vow
concepts.description: Sati's twelve-month calendar: no priest, no fire, no counts, no failure clause; named for a tithi group it barely uses

concepts.title: I Am Impure and Inauspicious
concepts.description: Shiva refuses to marry on the ground of his own standing, and calls marriage a great bondage; every charge in Daksha's later insult is conceded here first

concepts.title: Brahma Recruits Sati Herself
concepts.description: the fifth party approached in the marriage campaign, and the only one asked for nothing; she is told what she desires

concepts.title: The Newborn Who Spoke to Her Father
concepts.description: Devi confounds the birth chamber to speak to Daksha alone, excluding her mother by name, and delivers a receipt rather than an explanation

concepts.title: You Are Not a Man or a Woman
concepts.description: the gods' apophatic hymn negates species, all three sexual categories and existence, then furnishes the room it cleared; the one local survivor is the three Shaktis

concepts.title: She Divided Herself Into Sarasvati and Lakshmi
concepts.description: one prior goddess divides herself into three and the three highest gods marry the three forms; a second unqualified origin the volume never reconciles

concepts.title: When He Comes and Asks for Alms
concepts.description: Daksha frames the bestowal of his daughter as bhiksha; Shiva complies at the correct muhurta wearing every ornament Daksha later calls disgusting

concepts.title: Named Uma by Instruction
concepts.description: the gods choose the goddess's name and the father announces it, and in a volume that derives everything her name gets no derivation

concepts.title: Brahma at the Wedding Fire
concepts.description: the officiant floods his own sacrificial fire to make smoke, lifts the bride's veil and sheds four drops, then conceals it; premeditated and narrated as a lapse

concepts.title: The Penance Was to Keep Telling It
concepts.description: the confession is the penance, discharged by repetition and absolving the listener, which explains which of Brahma's crimes he narrates and which he deletes

concepts.title: Kill Anyone Who Looks at Her
concepts.description: Vishnu's unprompted blanket death penalty covering desire on hearsay, granted with a laugh and collected on within the same chapter

concepts.title: Shiva Argues Against Non-Difference
concepts.description: the supreme brahman raises the empirical objection to non-dualism and is corrected in public by Vishnu; the narrator patches it in five words

concepts.title: Brahma Becomes the Bull
concepts.description: a sentence with no suffering in it: he transforms himself into Shiva's mount, is named Rudrashira and scripted to explain it, on taxonomic rather than moral reasoning

concepts.title: If a Person Tries to Harm Another
concepts.description: the volume's only explicit moral, spoken by the offender about himself before he narrates the crime, and contradicted by the volume's own plot

concepts.title: The Four Clouds of Dissolution
concepts.description: Brahma's four drops become the standard four pralaya clouds, live in front of the assembled gods; the apocalypse machinery given a shameful origin

concepts.title: The Boon for the Barren and the One-Eyed
concepts.description: the officiant's fee paid in full to the man who sabotaged the ceremony, spent half on a tirtha at the scene of his crime and half on unfortunate women, free

concepts.title: She Asked for a House
concepts.description: Sati asks twice for a residence and is answered with four mountains and wish-fulfilling trees; no house is ever built, and she dies partly for want of anywhere to return to

concepts.title: He Sent the Ganas Away
concepts.description: the first act of the marriage is emptying the household, with a recall triggered only by Shiva's memory; the retinue returns only to escort Sati to the sacrifice

concepts.title: Shiva Summons Kama Himself
concepts.description: the god who swore Shambhu could not be deluded, and was cursed for trying, is summoned voluntarily and put to work; immune, pierced, client in twelve chapters

concepts.title: He Did Not Sacrifice or Think of the Brahman
concepts.description: ten thousand divine years of suspended practice by the being all the practice is for, recorded in one unemphatic sentence and never remarked on

concepts.title: Sati Ends the Idyll
concepts.description: satiety producing non-attachment in a volume that manufactures it by deprivation; the only decision in the marriage that is hers, and the Khanda's doctrine follows from it

concepts.title: The Nine Limbs of Bhakti
concepts.description: nine unranked doors with no counts, and no difference between bhakti and jnana; the volume's second complete framework for devotion, and it does not match the first

concepts.title: Nandi Beat Vyasa Out of Kashi
concepts.description: this text's own compiler flogged out of a holy city for an opinion about rank, cited as one of four proofs that Shiva is controlled by his devotees

concepts.title: The Consecration of Vishnu
concepts.description: Shiva builds the throne, crowns Hari, bows first and grants everything including Goloka, keeping one clause: Rudra is my heart and I am he

concepts.title: The Taxonomy That Will Not Sort
concepts.description: six classificatory cuts of bhakti in four sentences, none composing, one a number with no contents; five vocabularies stacked and exactly one worked out

concepts.title: Sixteen Maidens From Each Category
concepts.description: the only ceremony in the Khanda described by inventory rather than adjective; the volume counts when a rite's legitimacy is in question

concepts.title: Daksha Curses the Insignia
concepts.description: the Shaiva costume pronounced as a curse, the same four marks Yama's servants may not cross; nine charges for one discourtesy

concepts.title: I Have Not Been Cursed
concepts.description: Shiva declines the insult on positional grounds and corrects the gana who defended him, never addressing Daksha

concepts.title: What Is the Need for Rudra?
concepts.description: Daksha's real argument is redundancy rather than contempt, and the volume never answers it in the room where it is made

concepts.title: Kama Reports That It Cannot Be Done
concepts.description: the earliest of four accurate objections and the only one from a party who ran the experiment first; two campaigns, a named control group, a triple oath, a correct forecast of his own death, and compliance anyway

concepts.title: The Maras Born From a Sigh
concepts.description: an army exhaled from Brahma's frustration whose whole vocabulary is kill, named by transcribing its own noise; the sixth instance of the created-being formula and the only one asked by a third party

concepts.title: My Body Was Not Reduced to Ashes
concepts.description: a non-event explained twice and incompatibly by the man spared, with the deflating third reading supplied by the same speaker and never offered as a reason

concepts.title: Pierced by Kamas Arrows After All
concepts.description: Brahma concedes the checkable claim to purchase the uncheckable one and closes Daksha on a report about Shiva's inner state that flatly contradicts chapter 61 in the same narration

concepts.title: Nandis Curse of the Brahmanas
concepts.description: a curse whose every item lands on the receiving end of a transaction, assembled from Gita 2.42-43 per Debroy, widening from named persons to anyone who abandons Shiva, then voided and never deleted

concepts.title: Dadhichi Walks Out
concepts.description: the only guest who notices the absence, the only objector in the Khanda who refuses to comply, and the one whose departure the host reclassifies as purification

concepts.title: Eighty-Six Thousand Ritvijas
concepts.description: the volume's one rite described by figures rather than adjectives, staffing four functional priestly classes at a scale with no ritual function, because the roster is the argument that Shiva is surplus

concepts.title: She Heard It From a Passing Woman
concepts.description: exclusion discovered from passing traffic rather than communicated, reaching her third-hand through four people none of whom is family, with the reason withheld by her husband

concepts.title: Worse Than Death to Go Uninvited
concepts.description: Shiva states the mechanism of Sati's death to her face as a general rule, names the verbal weapon precisely, and grants permission four exchanges later without the one fact she lacked

concepts.title: Sixty Thousand Ganas Went With Her
concepts.description: an escort of status goods answering the danger he named rather than the one he described, unbriefed; twenty thousand kill themselves when she burns and the rest are routed by Bhrigu's Yajur Veda mantras

concepts.title: He Doesn't Have a Lineage
concepts.description: Daksha's charge sheet is the vault's own outsider-Shiva portrait with the valence reversed, and his one wholly accurate claim, that Brahma urged the marriage, is answered by nobody

concepts.title: Slice Off the Tongue
concepts.description: the only doctrine Sati issues: a two-tier rule with a capacity test, neither tier of which involves answering the criticism, announced after the decision it justifies

concepts.title: Sati Burns Herself by Yoga
concepts.description: not a leap into a fire but a named yogic procedure, prana and apana balanced and udana raised through four stations; nobody touches her, and the later institution that took her name has none of its elements here

concepts.title: Bhrigu's Mantra Beats the Ganas
concepts.description: a Shaiva army routed by correct Vedic procedure in a Shaiva text, covered by a single clause attributing the defeat to Shiva's own wishes

concepts.title: Virabhadra and Mahakali From One Hair
concepts.description: Shiva summons an independent witness before acting, the only verification in the whole Khanda; then one strand splits into two beings and only one of them is ever instructed

concepts.title: Teeth for Smiling, Eyes for Winking
concepts.description: punishment indexed to micro-expressions, and the only two offences the text bothers to justify are the two smallest

concepts.title: They Agreed to Fight
concepts.description: the Khanda's headline duel is negotiated in advance by both combatants, choreography and exit included, and the next chapter reports it as a real defeat with no acknowledgement

concepts.title: I Did Not Cause the Breaking Up
concepts.description: an unprompted denial of a commission the same narrator reported eleven chapters earlier, in a room where three witnesses to it are all asking the denier for something

concepts.title: Six Disclosed Repairs
concepts.description: the translator's own log of six places he changed or expanded the text; flagged versus fixed governs every seam claim in this build, and six is a floor rather than a ceiling

concepts.title: Vishnu Knew and Went Anyway
concepts.description: he names the curser, the event, the outcome and his own survival before any of it, then commits to the course that produces all four; the fifth accurate forecast in the Khanda and the one that removes the last variable

concepts.title: The Settlement, Itemised
concepts.description: the volume's only reparations schedule, in which restoration tracks ritual function rather than harm, the remedies precede the inquiry, and Sati has no clause

concepts.title: Only Through Bhakti
concepts.description: the gods' own preceptor lists mantras, herbs, karma, the Vedas and mimamsa as incapable of knowing Isha; the volume's third complete framework for devotion and the only one with no practice attached

concepts.title: He Resorted to the Path of Ordinary People
concepts.description: the Khanda's closing paragraph grants Shiva his only interior state and withdraws it in the next sentence; the third position on whether Shiva can be moved, and the one that dissolves the question

concepts.title: Devotion Runs Through Vishnu
concepts.description: the closing doctrine makes the rival load-bearing and adds Volume 1's only symmetrical exclusion, binding both constituencies; every term of the settlement issued from the winner's chair

concepts.title: Kshuva and the Varna Argument
concepts.description: the Khanda's catastrophe traced back to two friends arguing whether a brahmana outranks a king; the king cites shruti, the narrator overrules him naming no passage, and a fist and a vajra settle it

concepts.title: Dadhichi's Three Boons
concepts.description: every boon is a negative image of one past injury; the received tradition has the vajra made from his bones as self-sacrifice and here it is put into them on request, for a private quarrel

concepts.title: The Mahamrityunjaya Mantra
concepts.description: the Khanda's fullest liturgy, taught over a corpse by the preceptor of the asuras and claiming Vedic provenance, which Debroy flags as an expansion of the standard rather than the standard

concepts.title: Vishnu in the Brahmana's Disguise
concepts.description: a deception the narrator names as one, detected in a minute, after which Vishnu praises the man who exposed him, shrinks the ask to a performance, and escalates when refused

concepts.title: The Sudarshana Is Shiva's
concepts.description: Vishnu volunteers that his own discus originated with Shiva while petitioned for help; nobody takes the weapon, what is removed is the entitlement to it

concepts.title: The Omen Catalogue
concepts.description: portents of all three types, understood by everyone, naming no remedy; the actionable warning was refused three chapters earlier and this one produces patron-seeking instead of correction

concepts.title: The March, Counted
concepts.description: a census whose unit dissolves partway through and which nothing downstream consumes; the army resembles Shiva and is emitted from his body rather than equipped

concepts.title: The Four Kinds of Devotee
concepts.description: a ranking by contingency rather than virtue, with no route between the rungs, delivered to a man already punished in order to make his punishment a lesson

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster I, the Parvati Khanda opens (2026-08-10)

concepts.title: Disabled by Maya, Then Held Liable
concepts.description: the Khanda's spine: agents are impaired by Shiva's maya and then charged for the act the impairment caused, four times in twenty-four chapters, with the curser impaired too

concepts.title: The Test That Shiva Commissioned
concepts.description: the prize authors the exam and briefs seven sages to lie; they defame his own messenger, and the commissioned lie contains the volume's most damning account of Sati's abandonment

concepts.title: The Arrow That Failed and the Archer Who Burned
concepts.description: the concentration breaks before Kama acts, Shiva names the transgression as his own, the arrow is declared to have failed, and Kama is incinerated anyway

concepts.title: You Are Prakriti, I Am Purusha
concepts.description: Parvati runs Samkhya against Shiva's Vedanta and is answered by relocation rather than refutation; the narrator scores it a draw and the plot scores it a defeat

concepts.title: One Who Does What Should Not Be Done
concepts.description: Nandi names the override and Shiva confirms it: sufficient properly-performed devotion revokes a stated position, which makes every prohibition in the volume a starting price

concepts.title: The Customary Practices of the World
concepts.description: an indemnity clause appearing six times in twenty chapters, attached only to acts the doctrine cannot absorb and never to anything creditable; licence rather than suppression

concepts.title: The Ascetic Heat That Does Not Care Who Is Burning
concepts.description: the demon's austerity and the goddess's austerity produce indistinguishable effects in matched scenes eight chapters apart, and the volume never marks the parallel

concepts.title: Taraka Abandons Heaven When Asked
concepts.description: the volume's first altered decision after ninety-five chapters of accurate warnings changing nothing, and it belongs to the antagonist; it trades in terms rather than knowledge

concepts.title: The Palm Line That Cannot Be False
concepts.description: an accurate forecast whose remedy is revaluation rather than escape; the prediction comes true exactly, the family's conduct changes completely, and the two never conflict

concepts.title: Two Etymologies for Uma
concepts.description: two incompatible origins for one name fifteen chapters apart, both marked as the origin, unflagged by a translator who flags inconsistencies constantly

concepts.title: The Conduct Followed by Bad Yogis
concepts.description: the narrating voice labels its own god's misogynist refusal as substandard practice, before the speech, with none of the protective clause it normally supplies

concepts.title: Bhauma and the Substitute Mouth
concepts.description: a child born from sweat cries instead of asking for a task and the earth takes the slot; seventh created-being instance, and the slot has never once gone unfilled

concepts.title: The Mare-Headed Fire, Held Until the Deluge
concepts.description: divine rage as a conserved substance that outlives its target, cannot be extinguished, and is stored under contract in the ocean until the end of the world

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster J, part 1 (2026-08-10) — Volume 1 now 100% read

concepts.title: The Slander That Shiva Wrote
concepts.description: a disparagement kit deployed four times in twenty chapters, three of them by Shiva himself, and a grieving mother reproduces its three figures in order; unflagged by the translator

concepts.title: Eight Arguments and a Pretty Face
concepts.description: eight authorities argue correct theology at Mena and all eight fail; a change of face succeeds in one sentence containing no retraction

concepts.title: The God With No Gotra
concepts.description: Shiva cannot answer the routine lineage question at his own wedding and the silence is covered by a veena he arranged through Narada

concepts.title: Criticize Yourself Instead
concepts.description: two gods refuse to slander Shiva so Shiva slanders himself, and the motive is keeping the Himalayas' mineral wealth on earth

concepts.title: Brahma at the Wedding
concepts.description: the same offence as Kama's under the same impairment, pardoned rather than punished, and the variable is whether a court was present to perform praise

title: Shiva Purana Vol. 1 (tr. Bibek Debroy) DEEP INGEST — Cluster J, part 2 (2026-08-10) — CLUSTER J COMPLETE

concepts.title: The Disguised Test
concepts.description: four disguised tests in eleven chapters, and in at least two the tester states outright that he already knew the answer; what the scenes produce is testimony rather than knowledge

concepts.title: A Daughter Given to Avert a Threat
concepts.description: extortion under threat of incineration, advised as policy by the king's own gurus, and retold to Himalaya as a model of a father who saved his lineage

concepts.title: Padma's Curse and the Four Yugas
concepts.description: the four-yuga decline of dharma attributed to one woman's irrevocable curse, converted by her into a schedule with a reset because it could not be withdrawn

concepts.title: The Pavilion of Artificial Gods
concepts.description: a wedding hall built to confuse, succeeding on the gods themselves, described by a narrator who reports his own counterfeit in the first person

concepts.title: The Goddesses at the Bedchamber
concepts.description: the volume's sharpest objection to itself, raised by Tulasi and dismissed by another goddess as women's prattle; the third disposal by renaming

concepts.title: Kama Comes Back and Apologises
concepts.description: a third irreconcilable revival, and the exonerated man spends his one boon asking pardon for a crime the text showed he did not commit

concepts.title: The Dharma of a Virtuous Wife
concepts.description: wifely submission taught to the mother of the universe, excused by the indemnity clause, with an exemplar list that includes the volume's two most disobedient wives

concepts.title: She Does Not Get a House
concepts.description: the standing check closes negative: a bedchamber in her father's house for four days, then his mountain, and a dowry of a hundred thousand cows containing no dwelling

concepts.title: Uttama-Bhakti — The Definition and Its Two Halves
concepts.description: Rūpa's one-sentence definition split into the characteristic that gives bhakti its nature and the two that fence it off from its neighbours

concepts.title: Ativyāpti and Avyāpti — The Two Faults of a Definition
concepts.description: the definition stress-tested from both sides at once: hired assassins who pass it, and Yaśodā who fails it

concepts.title: The Ādi Clause — What "And So On" Excludes
concepts.description: two words that exclude classical yoga and sāṅkhya from the category without calling either false

concepts.title: Three Jñānas, and Which One Bhakti Refuses
concepts.description: two kinds of knowledge are required and one is refused, on grounds of coherence rather than falsity

concepts.title: Āropa-Siddha, Saṅga-Siddha, Svarūpa-Siddha — Three Grades of Counting
concepts.description: devotion by attribution, by association, or by constitution; and the demotion of twenty-six virtues to retinue

concepts.title: Bhakti Is Produced Only by Bhakti
concepts.description: the causal closure that rules out ritual, knowledge, yoga, austerity and vows, and the firewood argument that saves the dry morning

concepts.title: Tādātmya — The Iron Rod and the Fire
concepts.description: how a function of Kṛṣṇa's own energy operates through senses the book calls unconscious, and why the image is a forge rather than a lamp

concepts.title: Why a Manufactured Goal Would Be Worthless
concepts.description: the tradition's own objection that a produced summit is an artefact, and the answer that nothing was ever made

concepts.title: Why Bhakti Must Be Three and Not Two — The Argument From What Still Hurts
concepts.description: the middle stage defended by a symptom: emotion already present, obstruction not yet cleared

concepts.title: Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura — The Man Who Refused the Title
concepts.description: three books before he left his teacher's house, five generations compressed into one verse, and an ācārya who never used the title

concepts.title: The Half-Syllable Crisis
concepts.description: a scholar at the water's edge at night because a syllable count would not resolve, and a revelation whose content is a bibliographic citation

concepts.title: Twenty-Three of Twenty-Seven
concepts.description: the book's own appendix discloses that only three of its twenty-seven texts carry Rūpa's compositional voice, and none of them are in the rasa half

concepts.title: The Jaipur Debate and the Govinda-Bhāṣya
concepts.description: the sampradāya wins every argued point, loses on a missing commentary, and writes the commentary

concepts.title: Parakīyā-Vāda and the Jurisdictional Exemption
concepts.description: the rule against paramour love conceded in full and declared never to have covered Kṛṣṇa, on grounds only one entity can satisfy

title: Cluster B — the ladder and its obstructions (Text 3)

concepts.title: The Nine-Stage Ladder — Śraddhā to Prema
concepts.description: the ādau śraddhā sequence, and the finding that association occurs three times in it and is numbered once

concepts.title: The Anartha Taxonomy — Sixteen Plus Four
concepts.description: four classes of obstruction by four, plus four by origin, and the fourth origin is devotional practice itself

concepts.title: Sukṛti — The Two Kinds of Merit
concepts.description: two closed currencies of merit, each spent in its own denomination, neither convertible into devotion

concepts.title: Three Grades of Perfected Soul — Nirdhūta and Mūrcchita Kaṣāya
concepts.description: perfection graded by residue, with Nārada as the example of both the top grade and the bottom

concepts.title: Sajātīya, Snigdha, Mahattara — The Three Tests for Association
concepts.description: matched in mood, affectionate, and further along; all three at once, and the match is the one nobody checks

concepts.title: Virakti Must Precede the Cloth
concepts.description: detachment as a symptom of an arrived state, and why the renunciant's dress can only report it

concepts.title: Three Gurus — Śravaṇa, Śikṣā, Dīkṣā
concepts.description: one office decomposed into three functions with three different cardinalities: many hearing-sources, several instructors, one initiator

concepts.title: Sarāga and Nirāga Vaktā — The Two Kinds of Teacher
concepts.description: the disqualifier is not error but durability: the influence of an attached speaker does not endure

concepts.title: Dīkṣā as Third Birth — Daikṣa-Janma
concepts.description: bell metal transmuted to gold, and the claim that after initiation a śūdra no longer remains one

concepts.title: The Name Needs No Initiation, and the Mahājanas Took It Anyway
concepts.description: the tradition's most democratic verse and its most gatekept practice, both quoted approvingly, neither withdrawn

concepts.title: Guru-Sevā and the Asymmetry of Displeasure
concepts.description: the teacher can cover for the Lord's displeasure and not the reverse, and the corrective imported to stop that becoming worship of a man

concepts.title: When a Guru Must Be Abandoned
concepts.description: six conditions under which abandonment is enjoined rather than permitted, and the re-initiation clause that undoes the singularity

title: Clusters D and E — the sixty-four limbs and the offence architecture (Texts 4-7)

concepts.title: The Sixty-Four Limbs — Architecture, Not List
concepts.description: twenty items plus forty-four expansions plus five supreme, and the enumeration that yields sixty-five unless two are silently merged

concepts.title: Ekādaśī Tithi Mechanics and the Substitute Faster
concepts.description: one second of the previous lunar day voids the observance, and a fire-maintaining brāhmaṇa may appoint someone else to fast for him

concepts.title: Tulasī as Person, Not Plant
concepts.description: consent requested before the leaves are picked, and a plant who holds a gate over every food offering in the system

concepts.title: The Marks That Work Without Faith
concepts.description: clay on the forehead yielding imperishable results with rites, mantra, faith and timing all explicitly cancelled

concepts.title: The Six Limbs of Śaraṇāgati
concepts.description: surrender decomposed into two decisions, two beliefs and two admissions, and the appointment most practitioners never make

concepts.title: Three Kinds of Vijñapti
concepts.description: three prayers of ascending presupposition, of which exactly one is honestly available to you

concepts.title: Nāma-Saṅkīrtana Above Smaraṇa
concepts.description: the contemplative ladder inverted: remembrance has an entry requirement, chanting has none, and loud beats soft a hundredfold because of the hearers

concepts.title: Nāma Is Not in the Shape of Letters
concepts.description: the descent through the hlādinī-śakti, with letters arriving last and the mind demoted to a stop on the way to the mouth

concepts.title: Kārttika as the Creditor Who Forgives
concepts.description: a month that considers and bestows, and the clause where God withholds devotion because devotion binds him

concepts.title: Dhāma-Vāsa and the Māyāpura Claim
concepts.description: three residence limbs at three tiers, and a four-word sentence that extends the qualifying district six hundred miles

concepts.title: The Ten Prohibitions as Limbs of Devotion
concepts.description: abstention counted as cultivation, with nivṛtti sitting inside a list of things to do

concepts.title: Renouncing Many Disciples, Many Books, Many Projects
concepts.description: Jīva forecloses the growth defence by name, and this funded work of exposition sits inside the verse that forbids exposition as livelihood

concepts.title: Why the Demigods Must Not Be Blasphemed
concepts.description: worship as an exact readout of the worshipper's guṇa, and a corridor with a named offence on each wall

concepts.title: The Supreme Limbs and Their Conditions
concepts.description: five best practices, each carrying a condition whose failure inverts rather than weakens it

concepts.title: The Thirty-Two Sevā-Aparādhas
concepts.description: court etiquette written as scripture, ending in the one offence that only competence can commit

concepts.title: The Ten Nāma-Aparādhas
concepts.description: two of the ten are not acts but conclusions, and they are the two a sincere sceptic actually reaches

concepts.title: Nāma Forgives What the Deity Does Not
concepts.description: a three-tier hierarchy of recourse with nothing above its floor, and the Name ranked more merciful than the deity

title: Cluster F — vaidhi and raganuga, the problem of greed (Texts 8-11)

concepts.title: Vaidhī-Bhakti as Devotion Under Fear of Scripture
concepts.description: a category defined by what its members lack, running on fear, with the whole rule-code demoted to servants of two sentences

concepts.title: Lobha Cannot Be Produced by Argument
concepts.description: the book's load-bearing page: entry disqualifies itself if reasoning produced it, and the method exists only in the reasoning's own scripture

concepts.title: Sādhaka-Rūpa and Siddha-Rūpa: Two Bodies, One Practice
concepts.description: two registers following two different exemplar-sets, and the compound extension on which Ekādaśī survives

concepts.title: Five Types of Rāgānuga-Sādhana
concepts.description: practices sorted by fit with one's mood, four verdicts meaning keep, and one category dropped though scripturally prescribed

concepts.title: The Diminution Clause
concepts.description: limbs may be lost without damage and principal limbs may not; three items are load-bearing and sixty-one are not

concepts.title: Vidhi-Mārga Terminates at Dvārakā
concepts.description: a path with a stated destination that is not the one its practitioners want, capped by a lens rather than by a shortfall

concepts.title: The Sahajiyā Error: "I Am Lalitā"
concepts.description: the correct practice with one relation altered, collapsing into the non-dualism the whole system was built to refuse

concepts.title: Rāgānuga Must Pass Through Gaura-Līlā
concepts.description: a mandatory intermediary who is simultaneously the object and someone visibly lacking it

concepts.title: Rūpa Kavirāja and the Smaraṇa-Only Heresy
concepts.description: expelled by Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's daughter; his three claims remove exactly the three limbs the tradition names indispensable

concepts.title: Bhāva-Bhakti as a Ray of the Sun of Prema
concepts.description: not a smaller love but a portion of the real one, composed of two divine potencies, with `mahābhāva` already inside the definition of its first rung

concepts.title: The Nine Symptoms of Bhāva
concepts.description: four absences and five appetites, and a king who begged in the cities of the kings he had beaten

concepts.title: Ratyābhāsa: Pratibimba and Chāyā
concepts.description: the state you catch off the room, and Jīva's objection that a reflection should vanish when the source leaves

concepts.title: Prema Does Not Abandon Its Earlier Stages
concepts.description: the sāṅkhya objection from a sugar refinery, and a childhood body that relocates to another universe rather than ceasing

concepts.title: Sneha, Māna, Praṇaya, Rāga, Anurāga, Bhāva, Mahābhāva
concepts.description: the root text and the commentary give different orders on facing pages, and the term the compression drops is the one that does not fit its axis

concepts.title: Mamatā as the Marker of Prema
concepts.description: love graded by a claim of ownership over God, in a corpus whose neighbours all treat mine-ness as the thing to remove

concepts.title: Bhakti-Rasa: The Five-Component Machine
concepts.description: one standing ingredient and four operators, of which only the environmental one is a lever a practitioner can reach

concepts.title: Viṣaya and Āśraya: The Two Supports
concepts.description: one fixed object and unlimited vessels, and what that fork let the taxonomy become able to see

concepts.title: The Heart Typology: Gold, Cotton, Ocean, Pond
concepts.description: drop a mountain in the ocean and nothing happens: visible ecstasy as a measure of the container rather than the contents

concepts.title: The Sixty-Four Qualities in Four Tiers
concepts.description: fifty shared with great souls, five with Śiva, five with Nārāyaṇa, and four left over: divinity established by subtraction, and the residue is all sweetness

concepts.title: Four Nāyaka Types, and Kṛṣṇa's Vices as Virtues
concepts.description: malicious, proud, deceitful, angry, fickle and boastful, conceded as faults and counted as virtues on grounds of scene-fitness

concepts.title: The Fourteen Uddīpanas and the Flute Measured in Inches
concepts.description: the machine's only accessible lever, catalogued to the eighth of an inch, with four of its items doubling as limbs

concepts.title: Five Intensities: Dhūmāyita to Sūddīpta
concepts.description: a scale whose lower rungs measure suppression and whose upper rungs count symptoms, joined by a fire metaphor

concepts.title: The Prāṇic Physiology of Ecstasy
concepts.description: mind submits to the vital air, the vital air meets the five elements, and eight symptoms follow; the one-way direction is doctrinally load-bearing

concepts.title: The Seven-Rung Scale of Who Is Weeping
concepts.description: one continuous Sanskrit scale from eternal associate to God-hater, printed in English as three plus four; identical tears, seven verdicts

concepts.title: Mṛti That Is Not Death, and Āvega's Eight Causes
concepts.description: inherited stage-directions with an umbrella still attached, and two pathological terms disclaimed while two more are not

concepts.title: Sāmānya, Svaccha, and the Fixed Sthāyibhāva
concepts.description: the devotee who reflects whichever mood he stands beside, and the claim that which of the five you end in is set by whose company your practice matured in

concepts.title: Svārtha and Parārtha Rati
concepts.description: the gear that makes seven secondary rasas possible: a primary emotion recedes on purpose and feeds them from behind

concepts.title: Kevala and Saṅkula Rati: Mixed Devotees
concepts.description: almost none of the named exemplars is a pure case, and the mixture is handled by one ranking clause and then never used

concepts.title: The Accretion Model: Śānta to Mādhurya
concepts.description: each rung keeps everything below it, on the ether-to-earth model; and two independent indicators that the bottom rung has a different object
